_comment_: P4-A: per-seat capacity map. Replaces the legacy single '4 Devin workers' cap with per-provider + per-model caps, a RAM governor, and a metered-seat class so prepaid-quota seats are exhausted before paid-per-token ones.
_comment_order: Selection order (fleet-ops#387): free lanes first, then prepaid-quota alternating (never stack), then metered last. prepaid_providers_in_order is expiry-first among prepaid (devin -> cursor -> cline -> ollama). Implemented in seat-lib.sh pick_seat; this file is data only. Classes are free / prepaid-quota / metered. subscription is accepted as an alias of prepaid-quota.
_comment_ram_governor: ram_gb_per_worker=1.5 (2026-08-27, fleet-ops#489). The governor is sized on the TYPICAL worker, not the worst case: admission keeps cgroup memory.current (honest cgroup cost), using p95*3 clamped to the 1.5 GB ceiling. The 2026-08-26 sample (fleet-ops#202) had memory.current p95=822.6 MB (p95_bytes=862556160) and process VmRSS p95=35 MB; the 2026-08-27 rolling sample is memory.current p95=1163.1 MB and process VmRSS p95=2.8 MB. Both p95*3 exceed the 1.5 GB ceiling, so lanes stay tight (~4). /proc/pressure/memory some avg10 was 1.53. fleet-ops#489: admission keeps using memory.current; the formula is now ram_gb_per_worker = min(memory.current p95 * 3, 1.5) = 1.5. This undercounts process VmRSS on purpose, because process RSS is not what the cgroup charges. Re-measure both with bin/ram-metric-compare (heartbeat section 14). The 1.28 that was here before 2026-08-26 was the median of completed-unit MemoryPeak (n=14, p95 4.4 GB, max 4.8 GB) - i.e. sized for the worst case, which the comment said was correct until per-worker caps existed. Now they do: MemoryHigh=3G throttles one worker, MemoryMax=6G is the hard stop, TimeoutStartSec=45min kills a wedge, and systemd-oomd kills at 80%/60s. The tail is bounded by the cgroup, not by a pessimistic per-worker budget, so a single 4.8 GB outlier throttles rather than taking the box into swap. Mechanical re-measurement: `bin/ram-measure` (also wired into fleet-heartbeat-tier1 section 14, history at ~/.local/state/ram-measurement/ram-measurement.json, rolling 10 runs). A re-derive of this number is `ram-metric-compare` + jq over ~/.local/state/ram-measurement/ram-metric-compare.json, then a PR; the heartbeat only measures, it never edits this file. Per-task-weight cap: NOT applied. task_weight() in seat-lib.sh distinguishes heavy vs light packets, but the 4.8 GB outlier was a single failed worker, not a class of task (n=14: median 1.28, p95 4.4, max 4.8 - the tail is one data point). Live heavy workers measure 0.8 GB. Revisit if the rolling ram-measure history ever shows heavy-class p95 sustained > 3 GB.

_comment_quota_bench: quota_bench_default_s (fleet-ops#90): fallback bench window in seconds used by seat-lib.sh mark_seat_quota_bench when a provider returns a quota/cap 429 whose error text carries NO explicit reset window. cline=604800 (ClinePass weekly cap), devin=900 (devin 15-min message rate limit). _comment_seat_roster: Nish 2026-08-25: ALL seats available everywhere so work never stops. Ten seats probed live and answering: devin, cursor, cline, ollama (Ollama Cloud), minimax, commandcode, openrouter, grok (SuperGrok via grok-cli), zenmux, hetzner. zenmux and hetzner carry FREE lanes as well as credits, and openrouter has free lanes alongside credits - none of them are metered-only, so none is capped 0. Only providers with no working credential stay at 0.
_comment_credits: zenmux and openrouter both carry FREE lanes AND paid credits (Nish, 2026-08-25). class=metered records that, but seat-lib.sh computes class_of() and then ignores it - pick_seat buckets by literal provider name, so both currently sit in the FREE bucket and their credits can be spent as if free. free_providers_in_order is the only working control until that is fixed (fleet-ops#42): free lanes first, credit-bearing seats last.
_comment_grok: grok cap=0 (2026-08-26): SuperGrok's subscription covers the grok.com app and the grok CLI, NOT the x.ai API. pi reaching api.x.ai/v1 with the CLI's own OAuth token returns 403 'You have run out of credits or need a Grok subscription'. pi also has NO registered grok-cli adapter ('No API provider registered for api: grok-cli'), so the CLI route is not reachable from pi either. Raising this cap requires either x.ai API credits (money - Nish only) or a pi custom-provider extension wrapping the grok CLI. Tracked in fleet-ops#41.
